svg.title: JavaScript on the Server!
svg.desc: Auto-playing 48s step-by-step explainer of "JavaScript on the Server!" (from img_2.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: Why Node.js is a natural fit for web servers, and what a server actually does with a request

g.text: What: Node gives JavaScript everything a web server needs, so the same language now runs in
the browser AND on the server.
Why: Result: fast, highly scalable network applications (back-ends) written in JavaScript.
Added: A new step shows what a server actually does with each request, which the slide

Why: A web server spends most of its time waiting (for the DB, disk, other APIs). Node waits
What: The language you use in the browser now also runs on the server, so one developer (or
team) can build the whole stack.
Why: Less context switching, shared code (e.g. one Joi schema in both), and JSON maps 1:1 to
Added: Server code is trusted: it holds DB passwords and API keys and must validate every
input. The browser never sees it.

What: Every request goes through the same cycle: the server listens on a port, parses the
request, runs your logic, then sends back a status code and a body.
Why: Frameworks like Express only make this cycle shorter to write; the core http module
